subject: Regional constraints checklist — hosting options and next steps
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Erickson <tom.erickson@pacifichlth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-07T09:18:00-05:00
Subject: Regional constraints checklist — hosting options and next steps

Hi Tom,

Thanks for taking the time today — appreciated the context on PacificHealth's rollout across EU and APAC sites. Quick recap from our discovery and the specific items that will shape whether Hosted, Dedicated, or Private is the right path: 

- Primary workload: clinical note summarization and QA for inpatient units.
- Traffic profile: ~2k requests/min peak, mostly short prompts (avg 200 tokens).
- Latency SLO target: P95 < 400ms for patient-facing workflows.
- EU residency: Germany and France sites require patient records to remain within country borders (not just within EU).
- APAC: Singapore and Australia prefer regional residency but Singapore may accept cross-border processing if encrypted and covered by DPA addendum.

Quick deployment comparison (high level):
1) Hosted API (Redwood): fastest to get started; we have Frankfurt and London endpoints. Does NOT offer per-country legal guarantees out of the box — data is stored within region but not guaranteed to never leave a country.
2) Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool deployed in EU region with tenant isolation and contractual routing policies — can get closer to country-level guarantees under a commitment/SLAs.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): full control over where data is processed and stored, supports customer KMS/HSM, but requires an architecture workshop and ~4–8 week lead time.

Attachments: draft deployment matrix and SOC2 snapshot attached.

Open items for your team to confirm:
- Does Germany/France require absolute "data never leaves the country" or is "data processed and stored in the EU" sufficient?
- Are there any APAC sites that will insist on on-prem or country-only residency?
- Any procurement milestones (PO, security questionnaires, DPA redlines) we should know about that affect timeline?

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm the country-level residency requirement by Fri 2026-12-10.
- Redwood returns an updated recommendation and high-level SOW by Tue 2026-12-14.
- If Private is required, we schedule a technical workshop the week of 2026-12-21 to scope infra and KMS integration.

If helpful, I can reformat the attached matrix as a one-page decision table for your legal/procurement team.

Thanks,

—Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-deployment-matrix.xlsx, soc2-snapshot.pdf

From: Tom Erickson <tom.erickson@pacifichlth.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marta Alvarez <marta.alvarez@pacifichlth.com>
Date: 2026-12-07T14:03:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Regional constraints checklist — hosting options and next steps

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the clear recap — that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Germany/France: they currently require "data never leaves the country" (strict). That is the requirement for archival clinical records and any PII used in the training or retention. For transient inference (ephemeral tokens used only for immediate response), some sites may accept EU-only processing, but we need legal to confirm.

2) Singapore: the clinical teams are okay with cross-border inference if data is encrypted in transit and at rest and covered by a DPA clause; however, Ministry-level customers may insist on Singapore residency.

3) Australia: likely fine with regional processing (APAC) but we need to confirm with their IT security lead.

Given the Germany/France hard requirement, it sounds like Hosted alone will not satisfy them unless Redwood offers country-isolated processing. Can you confirm whether Dedicated capacity + routing policies could be contractually scoped to "never egress from DE/FR datacenters"? If that requires Private, we need that budgeted and scoped.

Also attaching our initial procurement timeline: PO by end of Q1 2027, security questionnaire back by mid-Jan.

- Tom

Subject: RE: Regional constraints checklist — procurement/legal input needed

Marissa / Aisha — looping you in on PacificHealth since this looks like it will hit legal/procurement quickly. Some notes from infra/security perspective:

- If Germany/France require "never-leave-country", our standard Hosted endpoints won't meet that. Dedicated capacity in those countries could be an option if we include contract language that prohibits replication/egress, but that may require an elevated SLA and a product addendum.
- Private (VPC/on-prem) is the only guaranteed path for strict country-only residency; it requires network/firewall design and KMS integrations for BYOK.
- Time: Dedicated + contract negotiation ~4–6 weeks. Private install (customers in-country infra) ~6–10 weeks depending on procurement and network readiness.

Action items for legal/procurement:
- Can legal draft a short country-residency SOW clause that we can propose to German/French customers?
- Pricing lead: need an indicative uplift for Dedicated with a contractual "no-egress" policy and for Private on-prem install (hours + travel).

I can pull existing language we've used for other EU customers — suggest we surface both a Dedicated-based solution and a Private solution with clear TOC and timelines.

—Ben

Tom,

Thanks — that clarity helps a lot. Next steps from Redwood's side: 

1) I'll coordinate with Ben and Legal to produce two discrete recommendations by Tue 2026-12-14:
   - Option A: Dedicated capacity scoped to Germany and France with a contractual no-egress clause (includes price uplift and timeline).
   - Option B: Private (VPC/on-prem) deployment for strict country-only processing (workshop estimate + timeline).

2) I'll attach a one-page decision table formatted for procurement and legal, plus the draft SOW language for residency.

3) Please confirm by end-of-day Fri 2026-12-10 whether Germany/France intention is absolute "never leave country" or if "EU only" is acceptable for ephemeral inference — that will determine whether Dedicated is viable without Private.

Attachments: procurement-checklist.docx (procurement milestones), and a link to the shared drive with the deployment matrix: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xExample
